stories.headline: AAP’s Satyendar Jain, DJB ex-CEO Udit Rai among 6 arrested in corruption case
stories.summary: The Anti-Corruption Branch of the Delhi government has arrested six people, including former Delhi Minister Satyendar Jain and ex-Delhi Jal Board CEO Udit Prakash Rai, in a corruption case. The case is linked to alleged irregularities in the upgradation of sewage treatment plants in Delhi. The arrested individuals also include Ankit Srivastava, a former contractual consultant at the Delhi Jal Board, and proprietors of private companies. According to the Anti-Corruption Branch, Udit Prakash Rai received a bribe of Rs 1.52 crore, which was used to purchase immovable property. The arrests were made in connection with an alleged corruption case involving the tendering process for sewage treatment plant projects of the Delhi Jal Board. The investigation is ongoing, and the arrests mark a significant development in the case.

stories.headline: US cites India on voter IDs, but are elections under Modi clean?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump cited India's electoral system, where all voters have valid photo IDs, to push for the passage of the Save America Act, which requires proof of citizenship for voter registration. Trump has been touting India's election system as a model for tougher voter-identification rules in the US. India's Election Commission has issued over 100 crore Electoral Photo Identity Cards to electors. The Chief Election Commissioner of India has also questioned the US' lack of photo ID requirements. Trump argues that tighter voter identification requirements are necessary to protect the integrity of US elections. The reference to India's electoral system has sparked questions about the cleanliness of elections under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, amid concerns about the fairness and transparency of the electoral process in India.

stories.headline: ‘If govt doesn’t demonstrate…': CJP issues big 'two-day' warning over FIRs on protesting students
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has issued a two-day warning to the government, threatening to convene its National Working Committee to decide on nationwide action if the government fails to demonstrate progress on withdrawing FIRs against protesting students. The CJP is demanding the immediate withdrawal of FIRs registered against students and other protesters, as well as the release of those detained. If the government does not meet these demands, the CJP has warned that it will launch a fresh nationwide agitation. The party had previously committed to resuming protests if the government did not honour its commitments made on July 25. The CJP has stated that it will respond with a massive peaceful protest soon if its demands are not met, indicating a potential escalation of tensions between the party and the government.

stories.headline: PM CARES spent just Rs 88 lakh of its Rs 8452 crore in 2024-25, put 93% in FD
stories.summary: The PM CARES Fund had a balance of ₹8,452.07 crore by the end of the 2024-25 financial year, with a sharp increase of nearly ₹1,279 crore from the previous year. However, the fund's expenditure during the year was significantly low, at just ₹87.85 lakh, which is roughly 0.001% of the total balance. The majority of the expenditure, ₹87.84 lakh, was spent on the PM CARES for Children Scheme, with the remaining ₹451 going towards bank and SMS charges. Notably, nearly 93% of the fund's balance was parked in fixed deposits, earning around ₹475 crore in interest. This marks a significant decrease in expenditure from the previous year, when the fund spent ₹15.60 crore, mostly on the same children's scheme.
